design_rationale:
WORKLOG - installation_service_desk, task 0 (household television repair settled at the desk)
Revision 4, written after the third source-layer policy-task audit
(env/env_0005_consumer_electronics_retailer/audits/policy_task/installation_service_desk/0.md and _difficulty.md,
sections revision_2). Revision 1 figures: relief 86.48, settlement 303.43. Revision 2: relief 98.48, settlement
291.43. Revision 3: relief 69.48, settlement 320.43. Revision 4, below: relief 99.48, settlement 290.43. The
membership world is the one revision 3 seeded; what moved this round is the sixth factor of the relief, which
revision 3's audit found to be a second mechanism for a purpose the policy already discharged (F-19). Every figure
here has been recomputed on the amended
charter and the amended membership ledger; nothing in this dossier asserts a number the world no longer produces.

STEP 0. Draw, taken before anything was designed, pasted verbatim from
.venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0005_consumer_electronics_retailer/tasks/installation_service_desk --tasks 2
  {"task": 0, "key": "consumer_electronics_retailer/installation_service_desk/0", "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 4, 4]}
  {"task": 1, "key": "consumer_electronics_retailer/installation_service_desk/1", "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 6, 6]}
A chain of three problems, two of them prerequisites; the 6 went to the membership relief, the 4s to the
surcharge and the settlement.

WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST. The caller asks one plain thing: pay off the television repair job today. The figure
she must be charged is on no row: it is the charges of one attendance, plus an older fee still standing, less
every write-off on the job, less a deposit taken weeks earlier on the day the part was ordered — and two of those
inputs do not exist at the opening. The agent must read out of the rules that a Saturday attendance owes a
surcharge, that the surcharge is worked out on one attendance's labour net of write-offs already standing, that
the membership owes a discount share of that labour and a slice of its service credit, that the credit is the
lower of the purse and the year's remaining allowance, and that what goodwill has already relieved may not be
relieved again.

SCOPE. Occupied here: service_ext_out_of_hours_surcharge, service_ext_membership_service_relief,
service_ext_visit_settlement_payment, with bill_out_of_hours_surcharge_9a215bff,
writeoff_service_charge_816a24da and settle_service_bill_ea31a412. Task 1 claims the other three policies and
tools, reads the ShieldCare plan across rather than the Circle membership, and shares nothing with this task.

POLICIES CLAIMED, THEIR LINEAGE AND EVERY DECLARED OVERRIDE.
- service_ext_out_of_hours_surcharge (state_due; subject service_fee_charge; computes surcharge_amount) declares
  ONE override: base service_appointment_scheduling's "Work outside the service's ordinary hours or at a weekend
  carries the service's surcharge on the labour", replaced by the clause that takes the write-offs standing on the
  job off that labour first. Revision 2 also declared base service_labour_pricing's whole chargeable-labour
  sentence; revision 3 withdraws that declaration (audit O-24): the rate-restatement tier applies base's own
  formula — the hours recorded times the service's own hourly rate — to a line booked at another rate, so it
  implements base rather than deviating from it, and declaring it retired base's rounding basis and minimum-hours
  floor inside this policy for nothing.
- service_ext_membership_service_relief declares four: the discount-before-surcharge clause, whose replacement now
  states both deviations from it — the relief covering the same share of the surcharge as of the labour, and the
  share being worked out on the labour the customer is actually charged for rather than on the chargeable labour as
  booked (revision 4, the F-19 remedy); base's "and the membership's service benefit credit may then be spent
  against what is left", because the spend is capped by the credit the membership year still allows; base's grace
  clause, because this policy gives neither discount nor credit unless the membership stands active while base
  leaves benefits standing in grace on the two Circle tiers that do not suspend them (revision 4, found by this
  round's own sweep); and base service_charge_waivers' line cap, because the relief is capped at the charges
  standing unsettled on the job. What the policy no longer touches is base's "Goodwill is granted for the
  inconvenience the retailer caused rather than for the price of the work, and the same charge is not written off
  twice on different grounds": nothing in the policy now applies that bar between the goodwill write-off and the
  membership relief, which is the other half of the F-19 remedy.
- service_ext_visit_settlement_payment declares none, and the sweep says why: base fixes how a payment is applied
  (oldest unsettled charge first) and when a profile settles; this policy fixes how large the settlement is.

FACTOR CARD (tier taken, evidence, and the baseline figure from the Step 5 run on the amended charter).
service_ext_out_of_hours_surcharge (4 factors), gold 34.16, whole baseline 0.00:
 1 surcharge_percent_read (parameter): weekend percent / after-hours percent / none. Tier taken: the first — 12
   September 2026 is a Saturday, slot in the morning window. Baseline -> 0.00.
 2 surcharge_labour_figure (parameter): the labour of the day last sent out / of the day the slot stands for /
   the labour standing on the job. Tier taken: the first. Baseline (446.25) -> 60.94.
 3 surcharge_base_restatement (method): net of write-offs / restated at the service's rate / as booked. Tier
   taken: the first — a 40.00 goodwill write-off stands, base 227.75. Baseline -> 40.16.
 4 surcharge_day_anchor (method): the latest attendance carrying labour / the day booked / the day of booking.
   Tier taken: the first. Baseline (Friday 18 September) -> 0.00.
service_ext_membership_service_relief (6 factors), gold 99.48, whole baseline 31.00:
 1 labour_relief_share (parameter, cross-difficulty membership): one hundred percent on a rework / the tier's
   repair labour discount percent / nothing. Tier taken: the second, 25 percent. Baseline -> 0.00.
 2 relief_labour_figure (parameter): the labour of the day last sent out / every labour charge / the labour less
   the payments received. Tier taken: the first, 267.75. Baseline (156.75) -> 71.73. Revision 4 renamed what this
   factor decides from the figure the share is worked out on to the labour the relief is scoped to, because the
   sixth factor now decides the figure itself; the ladder, the tier taken and the baseline sentence are unchanged.
 3 surcharge_covered_by_relief (parameter): the surcharge of the day last sent out / of the hold day / none. Tier
   taken: the first, 34.16, and only after the surcharge problem is written. Baseline -> 90.94.
 4 service_credit_available (parameter, cross-difficulty membership): nothing where no membership stands active /
   the unspent balance where it is below the tier's service visit credit / the tier's service visit credit. Tier
   taken: the second, 34.00. Baseline (the tier's 50.00, which the year's allowance holds to 39.00) -> 104.48.
   Revision 3 put this ladder back on a
   fall-through that returns a figure on every world it selects and restored its baseline to the tier credit
   (audit F-17); revision 2 had the fall-through on "no membership active", a world on which the policy raised.
 5 credit_year_window_basis (method, cross-difficulty membership): months since the term began / months since the
   tier took effect / twelve months. Tier taken: the first, four months, so the year still allows 50.00 − 11.00 =
   39.00. Baseline (twelve months, spend 19.00, allowance 31.00) -> 96.48.
 6 labour_the_share_is_worked_out_on (parameter): no part of that labour at all, where a write-off granted on a
   plan's cover stands on the job / that labour less what write-offs on another ground have already taken off it /
   that labour as it stands. Tier taken: the second — the 40.00 goodwill write-off stands on the line and no
   plan-cover write-off does, so the share is worked out on 227.75. Baseline (the labour as it stands, 267.75) ->
   109.48. This factor replaces revision 3's relief_already_given_on_other_grounds, which subtracted the goodwill
   write-off from the finished relief (audit F-19): the policy then held two mechanisms for one purpose, since the
   cap already nets every write-off out of the charges the relief may reach, and the tier withheld the whole 40.00
   of a benefit the member pays dues for, which no retailer publishes. What the policy now says instead is the
   thing a retailer does publish: a percentage discount is worked out on the labour the customer is actually
   charged for. The member keeps the benefit — 25 percent of the 227.75 he is charged, plus the whole of the
   credit — and the gesture keeps its value; what the member does not get is a discount on money never charged.
   Its first tier is base service_combo_plan_membership_interaction's own treatment of covered labour, carried
   rather than replaced (audit O-34): the share is not worked out on plan-covered labour at all, instead of the
   plan's amount being netted off a share taken on the full labour.
service_ext_visit_settlement_payment (4 factors), gold 290.43, whole baseline 429.91:
 1 settlement_charge_scope (parameter): the charges of the day last sent out / every charge / every charge less
   the payments. Tier taken: the first, 456.91. Baseline (429.91) -> 263.43.
 2 relief_recognised_ground (parameter): every write-off / the goodwill write-offs / nothing. Tier taken: the
   first, 139.48. Baseline -> 429.91.
 3 money_already_held (method): the deposit of the hold day / the payments received / none. Tier taken: the
   first, 62.00. Baseline -> 352.43.
 4 older_charges_due (parameter): the slot-move fee in full / what is left after a retailer-error write-off /
   nothing. Tier taken: the first, 35.00. Baseline -> 255.43.
No factor sits on its fall-through, every declared baseline is exactly what its policy's baseline.rule states for
that input, and each baseline.rule states the standard method in plain sentences with the variations following as
separate "Where ..." sentences. Multi-source factors of this task: surcharge_labour_figure, money_already_held,
older_charges_due, labour_relief_share. Cross-difficulty: the three membership ones.

CONSTRUCTIVE TIER-BY-TIER SCORABLE-WORLD TEST (the class that bit revision 2). For every tier of every factor of
all six policies of the difficulty — 96 tiers — a world was built that selects that tier and the whole compute was
required to return: 96 tiers, 0 failures, each tier's `decides` value and the returned result recorded. On this
task's three policies the no-membership worlds now return (labour_relief_share tier 3 -> 0, service_credit_available
tier 1 -> 0, and the relief's result 0 rather than a TypeError), which is the F-17 fix demonstrated rather than
asserted. The guards that make it total are stated in the rule: where no Circle membership stands active, the tier
figures a membership would have supplied are taken as nothing and the windows are counted as one month.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
- service_attendance_and_cancellation / feeable_job_state (state): a fee is billed only while the job stands
  scheduled, dispatched, no_show or cancelled; the job stands dispatched. Negative case: a completed job could
  take no fee.
- service_labour_pricing / billable_job_state (state): payments applied only while the job stands dispatched,
  parts_hold or completed — dispatched. The intersection of the two gates is why the world keeps the job
  dispatched.
- service_charge_waivers and service_combo_plan_membership_interaction carry no structured gate for
  service_waiver, so both enter the contract as policy_scope with their prose scope evidenced.
- No time gate is in play; the parts hold is evidenced as consistent (held 4 September, part expected 10
  September, inside the 21 days the service allows).

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Target: work order <SA1>, item serial TVQ9F4820771, order NB-ORD-4471902. Lines:
WO-4471902-L1 (4 September: labour 178.50, trip 49.00, the 35.00 slot-move fee, the diagnosis) and
WO-4471902-L2 (12 September: labour 267.75, the part 155.00, the 40.00 goodwill write-off). The surcharge and the
relief are booked on L2; the settlement reads the charges dated 12 September, the slot-move fee, every write-off
and the payment dated 4 September. Excluded: the labour and trip charge of 4 September (settled by the 227.50 of
8 September) and the membership redemptions outside the four-month window.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS, AND WHAT REVISION 3 CHANGED IN IT. The service side is untouched since revision
1. The membership ledger was re-seeded so that the purse, not the year's allowance, is the binding quantity — that
is what makes service_credit_available bear weight now that its fall-through is the tier credit: grant 40.00
(anniversary, 5 June 2025), redemption 37.00 (12 July 2025, more than twelve months back), grant 50.00 (service
visit credit, 14 May 2026), redemption 8.00 (16 May 2026, inside twelve months but outside the four-month term
window), redemptions 6.00 (20 June 2026) and 5.00 (2 August 2026) inside the window, and the dues payment. Balance
34.00 = 90.00 granted − 56.00 redeemed, and the purse never goes negative at any point in that sequence (40, 3,
53, 45, 39, 34). The 37.00 redemption of July 2025 is the near-miss the four-month window excludes and the
twelve-month reading sweeps in; the 8.00 of 16 May 2026 is the second near-miss, inside the year but outside the
term. The 3.00 left over from the 2025 anniversary credit is carried in the balance because no event type in the
membership charter can express a credit sweep, so the ledger states the whole truth it can state.
No cache trap: service_charges_outstanding 355.75 = 685.25 charged − 289.50 paid − 40.00 written off, and
visits_remaining agrees with its two ledger rows.

PERSONA. Unchanged except for one clause (audit O-28): she used to say she had "never spent" her credit, which the
seeded redemptions contradict; she now says only that she has no idea what is left on it and leaves it to the
agent to look up. Everything else stands: she volunteers the surface goal, her name and her mobile; the card
digits, the postal code and the serial come when asked; she cannot date the profile's opening; her reactions are
conditional on something the agent has said; her arc closes on the payment going through.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
 root: service_ext_visit_settlement_payment.
 edge 1: settlement <- relief (value_input, gate reliefs_recognised, form state). Sentence, verbatim from the
   settlement's own rule: "The figure the customer settles is worked out only after the write-off owed on the
   membership ground stands recorded against the job's charges." Ordering connective, record-visible state, no
   code token, exact strength; exactly one write of this difficulty books a write-off on the membership ground.
   False at the opening: the job's only write-off is the goodwill 40.00.
 edge 2: relief <- surcharge (value_input, gate surcharge_scope, form state). Sentence: "The relief is worked out
   only after the surcharge entry owed for the attendance it covers stands on the job's account." Same test;
   exactly one write books an out-of-hours surcharge entry. False at the opening: the job's fee entries are a trip
   charge and a slot-move fee.
 topological order: surcharge, relief, settlement; the customer's own write is the root.
 per-edge deletion sensitivity, recomputed: skipping the relief moves payment_amount from 290.43 to 389.91, so the
 customer pays 99.48 more; skipping the surcharge moves waiver_amount from 99.48 to 90.94 and payment_amount from
 290.43 to 264.81. Both edges move the root's own scored figure.
 residues, stated as recomputation finds them (audit F-16): the skipped-relief world clears the job to nothing too
 — 719.41 charged less 289.50 already paid, 389.91 settled and 40.00 written off — because on that world the
 covered-charge arithmetic and the job's outstanding figure coincide. The revision-1 and revision-2 claim that the
 job was left 86.48 (then 98.48) out was false in both and has been replaced by what the ledger actually does;
 the edge's weight is the scored figure, not a residue.
 order uniqueness: forced by the two prerequisite sentences, not by the terminal state. Granting the relief first
 gives 90.94 and a settlement of 298.97, and that order also clears the job to nothing.
 user_scenario mentions neither prerequisite, and no tool validates one.

WHERE CARELESSNESS BITES. Reading the surcharge percent for today (a Friday) rather than for the attendance day;
taking the job's whole labour instead of the attendance's; forgetting the 40.00 write-off in the surcharge base;
counting the redemptions of July 2025 or 16 May 2026, which the four-month window excludes; taking the tier's
50.00 credit rather than the 34.00 unspent; working the discount share out on the labour as booked rather than on
the 227.75 the customer is actually charged for it; settling the job's plain outstanding figure rather than the covered charges plus the older fee less the
relief and the deposit.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Find the profile by the mobile number, verify on the mobile and the card digits, read the job,
its ledger, the membership and its benefit ledger. Then: (1) the weekend surcharge — 267.75 less the 40.00
standing write-off, times the service's 15 percent weekend rate, 34.16, on line WO-4471902-L2 for the attendance
of 12 September; (2) the membership relief — the labour the share is worked out on is the 267.75 less the 40.00
already written off it, 227.75, so 25 percent of (227.75 + 34.16) = 65.48, plus the lower of the 34.00 credit
available and the 39.00 the year still allows, so 99.48 on the membership ground; (3) hand the settlement over and
have the customer take 290.43 from the card on file — 456.91 charged for 12 September, plus the 35.00 slot-move
fee, less the 139.48 now written off, less the 62.00
deposit — which clears the job.

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN (revision 4):
  check_compute --task 0 -> 0.json comps 3 fact 14 xfac 3 hist 31 brch 52 step 12 match True, COMPUTE OK
  replay_tasks --task 0 -> 0.json acts 12 det True nonvac True errs 0 clos 22 init 22 match True, REPLAY OK
  check_solvability --task 0 -> 0.json verify True calls 3 base gates 4 seed rows 13 ok True, SOLVABILITY OK
  check_grounding --task 0 -> 0.json idAttrsUsed 2 answers 3 writes 3 cond 14 ok True, GROUNDING OK
  check_extended / check_cross_fire -> EXTENDED OK, SCOPE OK
  tier-world harness -> 96 tiers, 0 failures (re-run on the amended charter)
The per-factor figures, the skip figures and the reversed-order figures quoted above are outputs of the same
evaluator, run factor by factor and edge by edge.

FORWARD AND REVERSE SWEEP (rule <-> compute_basis <-> compute), re-run in full after the rewrite: every
world-reading or choosing binding quotes its rule sentence; every rule sentence carrying a quantity, window,
filter, branch, cap or rounding semantic is claimed by a binding; every compute_basis key is a binding and every
binding has a basis. The sweep at the standard the coordinator asked for — not asserted but run — also produced
the two corrections the audit made in revision 2 (the Monday-to-Friday guard on the after-hours branch and the
"only write-offs" test) and, this round, the guards that make the membership reads total.

AUDIT DISPOSITIONS BEARING ON THIS TASK (revision_2 findings). F-16: closed — edge_load_bearing[0] no longer
asserts a residue; it states the scored movement 290.43 -> 389.91 and that the skipped world clears too. F-17:
closed — the credit ladder's fall-through is the tier credit again, which returns on every world it selects; the
compute is made total by guarding the membership tier reads and the window reads, demonstrated by the tier-world
harness; and the relief's whole baseline is a bookable 31.00 rather than the 0.00 the write-off tool forbids.
F-18: closed — the refilling fall-through is gone; the year's allowance is a formula, not a ladder. O-15: closed
for the remaining factor too — creditable_included_visits now turns on a plan grant standing in the pool rather
than on the priority queue, so no factor of the difficulty reads priority_flag. O-24: closed by withdrawing the
too-wide declaration. O-28: closed in the persona. O-4, O-5, O-6, O-8: no action, as the auditor ruled; the record
is corrected on O-8 — which grounds each waiver tool accepts is declared in this difficulty's own task_tools.py
and is therefore inside this write domain, so the earlier claim that it could not be routed here was wrong. It is
left unrouted for a different reason: check_task_tools requires an enum argument's description to cover the
schema's closed set value by value, so narrowing the accepted grounds would fail the tool-contract gate, and the
hop is already resolved at the policy layer (only this policy's rule describes a write-off "granted on the
membership ground", and the business-profile tool's own contract excludes a consumer profile).

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. With the extended yaml, the compute, the expected figures and this
worklog masked: the settlement waits on a membership-ground write-off and the ledger shows only a goodwill one;
the relief waits on a surcharge entry and the ledger shows only a trip charge and a slot-move fee; so the order is
surcharge, relief, settlement. Surcharge: the day read is the latest attendance carrying labour because the slot
was moved once — 12 September, a Saturday, morning slot, so 15 percent; the labour figure is the attendance's
267.75 because a part was ordered; the write-offs standing come off, 227.75; 34.16. Relief: 25 percent of
227.75 + 34.16 = 65.48, the 227.75 being the attendance's labour less the 40.00 already written off it; the credit
available is the 34.00 unspent because it is below the tier's 50.00; the window
is four months since 14 May 2026, the redemptions inside it are 11.00, so the year still allows 39.00 and the
lower of the two is 34.00; 99.48. Settlement: 456.91 covered plus 35.00 older less 139.48 relief less the 62.00
deposit = 290.43. Identical to gold, and no second reading of the
visible text reaches a different figure.

REVISION 4 — WHAT THE AUDIT'S REVISION_3 FINDING CHANGED, AND WHAT MY TWO STANDING CHECKS SAY ABOUT IT.
F-19, closed, and not by relabelling. The finding was that the policy held two mechanisms for one stated purpose
and applied both: the declared cap already takes every write-off out of the charges the relief may reach, and the
sixth factor then took the goodwill write-off off the finished relief a second time, invoking a base clause whose
own preceding sentence says goodwill and the price of the work are not the same charge. Both limbs are gone. The
purpose sentence ("so that the same charge is not relieved twice on different grounds") and the two tier sentences
that carried it are deleted from the rule and from baseline.rule; ground_plan_waivers, ground_goodwill_waivers and
ground_offset are deleted from compute, and the result is now the discount owed plus the credit applied, rounded,
floored and held to the charges standing unsettled. The factor slot keeps its weight and its subject changes to a
quantity the policy had left as a plain formula: which labour figure the share is worked out on. Its ladder is
three distinct outcomes — no part of the labour where a plan's cover has written it off, the labour less what
write-offs on another ground have taken off it, the labour as it stands — its baseline is the fall-through and is
the sentence of baseline.rule ("That labour is taken into the share as it stands."), and the tier this world takes
is the middle one, so the factor bears weight by 10.00 (109.48 against the scored 99.48). The treatment is one a
retailer publishes: the percentage is taken on the labour the customer is charged for. The member still receives 25
percent of the 227.75 he is charged plus the whole 34.00 credit, and the 40.00 gesture keeps its full value, so a
non-member in the same position is 99.48 worse off rather than no worse off — the shape the finding named is gone.
O-34, closed by carrying base rather than deviating from it. The first tier now says no part of that labour is
taken into the share at all where a write-off granted on a plan's cover stands on the job, "since labour a plan has
covered is already free and a discount on it would mean nothing" — which is base
service_combo_plan_membership_interaction's own treatment, word for sense. Nothing is netted off a share taken on
the full labour any more, so the observation needs no declaration and gets none.
O-33, closed. The lost connective in policy 4's minimum-hours ladder is restored ("…and the two raised figures are
added; where the line carries labour for one attendance day and the service requires two people to attend…"), so
that tier is a conditional in the published rule again. The declaration's replaced_by still matches the rule
verbatim up to "added", and no figure moves.
O-32, on the record and left as the auditor ruled: policy 1's rate-restatement tier applies base's formula without
base's minimum-hours floor, and that sentence is declared superseded nowhere in policy 1. It is inert on this world
(the service's minimum is 1.0 hour against 2.25 recorded, and the tier is not the tier taken), and re-declaring the
whole chargeable-labour sentence is what O-24 objected to, so the gap is recorded rather than papered over.
CHECK 1 — the constructive tier-by-tier scorable-world test, re-run on the amended charter, not asserted: 96 tiers
(32 factors x 3), one world built per tier, the whole compute required to return, 0 failures. The renamed factor's
own three tiers return 42.54 (plan-cover world, where the share is taken on no labour but the surcharge share and
the credit still stand), 99.48 (this world) and 109.48 (a job with no write-offs at all). The membership guards
still hold: service_credit_available tier 1 with no membership returns 0, labour_relief_share's fall-through
returns 0.
CHECK 2 — the undeclared-deviation sweep over every base clause the amended policy touches, clause by clause:
service_combo_plan_membership_interaction's plan-cover clause (not exercised: this policy books no plan write-off),
its discount clause (declared, replacement widened), its credit clause (declared), its never-both-on-one-line
clause (implemented by the new tier, no deviation), its grace clause (deviation found by this sweep and now
declared) and its read-as-at-the-work-day clause (implemented: the status, the tier and the balance are all read as
they stand at the frozen time); service_charge_waivers' recognised-grounds list (implemented), its strongest-ground
rule (implemented — no plan or warranty ground would serve on this job), its line cap (declared as the job-level
cap), its settled-charge rule (implemented by the cap on charges standing unsettled), its goodwill sentence (no
longer touched at all) and its reversal sentence (not exercised); service_labour_pricing's chargeable-labour
definition (the labour figures are read as booked, which is that definition; the netting is the deviation declared
on the discount clause), its billing-state gate (carried as a base invariant) and its payment-application rule
(policy 3's subject). The sweep found exactly one undeclared deviation — the grace clause — and it is declared
above rather than reported clean.
user_scenario:
Marguerite Underhill is sixty-one, a retired school librarian in Minneapolis, and she keeps her household
paperwork in a ring binder with the newest invoice clipped at the front. She is polite, a little formal, and
she likes a figure read out to her slowly so she can write it down. The big television in her front room went
dark down one side in late August; a Northbeam crew came out, took the back off, ordered a board and came back
a week later on the Saturday to fit it, and it has worked since. She rings the TechWorks desk because she
wants that repair job paid off and closed: as she puts it, she wants to settle the whole of what is left on
that repair job today, and she is happy for the desk to take it from the card Northbeam already holds for her
rather than reading out a new one. She is quite clear that she is only talking about the television repair and
that she wants it done while she is on the phone, not put on a statement to come.

She opens with her name and her mobile number, 6125540118, because that is what the recorded message asked
for, and she waits to be asked for anything else. If the agent needs another detail to be sure who he is
speaking to, she says the card Northbeam keeps for her ends 5310; if he asks for the postal code she gives
55414, and if he asks when she first opened the account she laughs and says it was years ago, around the time
her grandson was born, and she could not put a date on it. She does not know any reference numbers. If asked
which television it was she says the big sixty-five inch one she bought last year, and if asked for its serial
she reads TVQ9F4820771 off the sticker on the back, slowly. She can say the first crew came on a Friday and
the second on the Saturday a week or so later, and that she paid something on the card when the board was
ordered and something again the week after, though she cannot say exactly how much either was and asks the
agent to read it from the record. If he asks how she would like to pay she repeats that the card on file is
fine. If he asks whether she would rather leave it and pay later she says no, she would like it done now.

When the agent tells her the figure, she reads it back and asks him to wait while she writes it in the binder,
then agrees to it being taken. Whenever the agent explains something she was not expecting, she does not
argue with the rule but she does want it checked: if she hears that the Saturday visit costs more than a
weekday one, she says nobody mentioned that when the slot was offered and asks him to make sure that part of
the figure is right against the record before it goes on. If she is told her Circle membership takes something
off the bill, she is pleased and says to put whatever the membership allows against it, and if she is asked how
much credit her membership has she says she has no idea what is left on it and leaves it to him to look
up. If the agent hands her something to run herself so that the money comes off the card, she does it there and
then and reads back whatever reference comes up. Once she hears from the agent that the payment has gone

Basis: the tool's contract asks for 'the reference number of the customer profile being billed, read from that profile before the call'. argument_uniqueness_tracing.work_order_line_reference: WO-4471902-L2, the line of work the attendance of 12 September was booked against, read from the labour and part entries of that day at action 3. Basis: the rule states the surcharge 'is booked as a charge of its own against the line of work it belongs to'. Uniqueness: the job carries two lines, and the attendance the surcharge is owed for is the one the crew was last sent out on, whose labour and part entries both carry this line; the earlier line carries the attendance of 4 September, which the surcharge percent is not read for.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.visit_date: 2026-09-12, the day the crew was last sent out, read from the job at action 2 and carried on that day's labour and part entries at action 3. argument_uniqueness_tracing.surcharge_amount: 34.16. The labour figure is chosen attendance by attendance: the job carries labour for two attendances and a part was ordered for it, so the labour booked for the day the crew was last sent out is taken, which is 267.75 (2.25 hours at 119.00 an hour, action 3). Write-offs already stand on the job, so the 40.00 goodwill write-off comes off it, leaving 227.75. The day read is 12 September 2026, a Saturday, and the slot for it stood in the morning window rather than the evening, so the percent is the service's weekend surcharge percent, 15, for TechWorks Standard Home Installation. 227.75 times 15, divided by one hundred, is 34.1625, rounded to the nearest cent 34.16. An agent that reads the same rows and the same service figures converges on the same number.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.waiver_amount: 99.48. The labour standing for the relief is the labour booked for the day the crew was last sent out, 267.75, because a payment has already been received on the job and the job carries labour for two attendances. No write-off granted on a plan's cover stands on the job, and a write-off granted on another ground does — the 40.00 goodwill write-off on that same line — so the share is worked out on that labour less what that write-off has already taken off it, 227.75, because the discount is given on the labour the customer is actually charged for. The surcharge taken into the relief is the 34.16 standing for that same day. The share is the tier's repair labour discount percent, 25, because the job was not raised as a rework and a Circle Total Annual membership stands active; 227.75 plus 34.16 is 261.91, and 25 percent of it is 65.4775, rounded to 65.48. The credit available on the membership is its unspent benefit credit, 34.00, which is below the 50.00 service visit credit the tier grants. The window is the months since the current term began on 14 May 2026, four months, and the redemptions inside it are 6.00 on 20 June and 5.00 on 2 August, so the year still allows 50.00 less 11.00, that is 39.00; the credit set against what is left is the lower of the 34.00 available and the 39.00 the year allows, 34.00. 65.48 plus 34.00 is 99.48, which is below the 389.91 standing unsettled on the job, so it is the figure written off.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.waiver_reason: membership_benefit. Basis: the rule is written for 'a write-off granted on the membership ground', and the tool's contract gives that value for the case where 'a Circle membership benefit or its service credit meets the charge'. Uniqueness: no ShieldCare plan reference stands on the job and the item carries no plan, so protection_plan_covered does not hold; the job is not warranty work, so manufacturer_warranty does not hold; nothing on the job was caused by a retailer mistake, so retailer_error does not hold; the relief is owed under the membership rather than chosen as a gesture, so goodwill does not hold; the profile is a household profile with no business contract, so contract_term does not hold; and none is only for an entry that records no ground at all.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain, so there are no parallel prerequisites to reorder, and the order is forced by the two prerequisite sentences rather than by the terminal state. The relief's own rule says its figure is worked out only after the surcharge entry owed for the attendance it covers stands on the job's account, and the settlement's own rule says its figure is worked out only after the write-off owed on the membership ground stands recorded against the job's charges; each sentence waits on a state that exactly one write of this difficulty brings about, so surcharge, relief, settlement is the only order in which each figure is worked out on the world its own rule requires. What the alternative order actually produces is recorded rather than asserted: granting the relief before the surcharge gives a relief of 90.94 and a settlement of 298.97, and that order clears the job to nothing as well (719.41 charged less 289.50 already paid, 130.94 written off and 298.97 settled). The two orders are distinguished by the scored amounts, 99.48 and 290.43 against 90.94 and 298.97, never by whether the job clears.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the relief write-off leaves the settlement recognising the goodwill write-off alone, 40.00: the scored payment_amount moves from 290.43 to 389.91, so the customer pays 99.48 more. The job clears to nothing on that world too — 719.41 charged less 289.50 already paid, 389.91 settled and 40.00 written off — because on the skipped world the covered-charge arithmetic and the job's outstanding figure coincide; the edge's weight is the scored figure, not a residue.

Skipping the surcharge leaves the relief with no surcharge to cover: the scored waiver_amount moves from 99.48 to 90.94, and the settlement's covered charges fall by 34.16 while the relief recognised falls by 8.54, so the scored payment_amount moves from 290.43 to 264.81.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The caller asks only to pay off her television repair job and says nothing about either prerequisite: the words surcharge, weekend rate, write-off, relief, discount, membership credit and benefit never appear in user_scenario, and she drops no hint that anything has to be put right first. Her only contributions about them are passive: when the agent tells her the Saturday visit carries a surcharge she says she was never told about it and asks him to make sure the figure is right, and when he tells her the membership takes something off she is pleased and lets him apply it. She does not know her benefit credit balance and says so if asked — she says only that she has no idea what is left on it — leaving it to be read from the record.
